thread:
elaine: Hey — running into 401s only when we build our Next.js app for SSR. Local dev (next dev) and plain node runs are fine. After build+start the SDK calls return 401. No token rotation on our side. Import is just `import Inference from '@redwood/inference'` and we pass process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY.

mike: Do you have a minimal repro or package.json? Which Next.js/node/bundler versions?

elaine: Repro here (private): https://git.internal/repro/rdw-bundle-401
package.json snippet:
```
"name": "customer-app",
"dependencies": {
  "@redwood/inference": "2.4.2",
  "next": "12.3.1"
}
```
Import line same as above. Node 16.15.0 in prod. Build produces `next start` serving SSR pages.

devx: Quick guess: bundler resolution + package exports conditional fields causing the runtime wrapper to be skipped. Some bundlers/Next SSR can pick the ESM entry and tree-shake the module initializer that attaches default headers. Can you paste the error/log from server?

elaine: Server log when request from SSR page hits API:
```
GET /api/generate 401 34ms - "Unauthorized: missing API key"
Error: 401 Unauthorized
    at makeRequest (/workspace/node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/esm/request.js:12:23)
```

mike: That stack path is interesting — it's pointing at dist/esm in the installed package when running under Node/SSR. Ideally SSR Node should resolve cjs. Next's webpack-ish resolver may prefer `import` conditions. Two quick repros:
- Try forcing the CJS entry: `import Inference from '@redwood/inference/dist/cjs/index.js'` and rebuild.
- Or pin SDK to 2.4.1 (older build) to see if regression.

elaine: Forced import to cjs path and rebuilt — SSR calls now succeed. So it's definitely resolver picking the esm entry that doesn't run the init.

jordan: Root cause summary from eng side: package.json exports used conditional exports like:
```
"exports": {
  "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
  "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
}
```
Next/webpack sometimes prefer the `import` path even for SSR Node builds, which means our ESM build (which relies on top-level side-effect to attach request defaults) was subject to tree-shaking/minification in certain toolchains and ended up not running the initializer when consumed that way. Result: no default Authorization header set and 401.

jordan: Short-term fixes:
- Workaround for customers: import the CJS entry directly (`@redwood/inference/dist/cjs/index.js`) or downgrade to 2.4.1.
- We're shipping a patch (2.4.3) that adds a small `exports` entry to force the package.json to expose the CJS entry for Node resolution and ensures the ESM build includes an explicit `init()` call. Also adding an explicit `main` and `module` fields to help bundlers.

mike: Also add to repro notes: some bundlers replace process.env.* at build time — verify your env var is not stripped. But since forcing CJS fixed it, this looks like exports resolution.

elaine: Nice, thanks. Can you link the GH issue/PR so I can watch? And is 2.4.3 expected today or tomorrow?

jordan: PR is https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482 (internal). Targeting a same-day patch release, ETA < 8 hours. We'll post release notes in #eng-releases. :thumbsup:

elaine: Confirmed 2.4.3 from our internal registry fixes the SSR 401. Thanks all! :tada:

mike: Great — marking as resolved on our side. If anyone hits a similar bundler edge, please share the build trace and package.json exports.
